report:
## Conclusion: the claim is false

There is **no reliable clinical evidence** that drinking boiled garlic water cures COVID-19. The specific “one bowl”/overnight-improvement recipe originated as a social-media rumor, not as a tested medical treatment. FactCheck.org found no evidence supporting it and reported that health experts rejected the claim.  
https://www.factcheck.org/2020/02/fake-coronavirus-cures-part-2-garlic-isnt-a-cure/

The World Health Organization states that, although garlic is a healthy food with some antimicrobial properties, **there was no evidence that eating garlic protected people from the new coronavirus**. A claim that boiled garlic water *cures* an established infection is even stronger and likewise unsupported.  
https://www.who.int/vietnam/emergencies/covid-19-in-vietnam/information/mythbusters

**What evidence might make the rumor sound plausible?** Garlic contains compounds such as allicin, and laboratory or general-health findings have prompted interest in possible antimicrobial or immune effects. But laboratory mechanisms, nutrition claims, or anecdotal recoveries do not demonstrate that a boiled-garlic drink clears SARS‑CoV‑2 or improves COVID-19 outcomes in people. I found no credible randomized clinical evidence supporting the cure claim.

In contrast, CDC clinical guidance recommends evaluating people at higher risk of severe disease for **authorized antiviral treatments**, which must be started promptly after symptom onset to reduce hospitalization and death—not substituting garlic water.  
https://www.cdc.gov/covid/hcp/clinical-care/outpatient-treatment.html

Garlic water may be consumed as food if tolerated, but it should not delay testing, medical advice, or indicated treatment. Seek urgent care for trouble breathing, persistent chest pain/pressure, new confusion, inability to stay awake, or bluish/gray lips or skin.
